_comment: Manual graph patches for the Tignes / Val d'Isère build. Applied by skiroute.build_graph after the automatic build. Keep entries here when OpenSkiData omits a real-world connection or geometry truncates a piste.

add_edges._comment: Digues is Tignes Le Lac's 'home run' — purely for skiing back to accommodation at end of day. The piste empties into the village road network next to Aquatignes, but OpenSkiData truncates the geometry ~260m short of the nearest graph node. Without this edge the run is a dead-end pocket and the router refuses to plot home routes that end on Digues.

Diebold piste continues from Verte bottom (249) → 3J top (264) — a 54m blue run section that OSM labelled 'Diebold' but mis-typed as skate. Reinstating as a proper run keeps the Diebold descent reading as one continuous piste from Funival top down to Daille bottom.
add_edges.name: Diebold

add_edges._comment: 53m mid-piste segment of Coupe du Monde (node 298 → Orange top 357) that OSM tagged as 'Run 125831' skate. Reinstating as a Coupe du Monde run keeps the descent continuous from Coupe du Monde top all the way to Daille bottom.
add_edges.name: Coupe du Monde

add_edges._comment: Pim Pam carpet lift in the Val d'Isère Solaise beginner bowl. Bottom = Madeleine bottom (node 225, 2516m), top = Solaise top (node 109, 2550m); 261m horizontal, +34m vertical. Closes the bunny-hill loop: ski down 'Run 68931' or 'Lac/Parc à Moutons' from Solaise top, ride Pim Pam back up. Missing from OpenSkiData; added manually. ~240s for the slow carpet ride.
add_edges.name: Pim Pam

add_edges._comment: Madeleine access piste, Madeleine Express bottom (97) → Madeleine bottom (225). 87m essentially flat green connector used to ski between the Madeleine Express chairlift and the bottom of the Pim Pam carpet. Replaces the existing skate.
add_edges.name: Madeleine

add_edges._comment: Reverse direction of the Madeleine access piste (225 → 97). Same gentle green; runs are stored as one-way edges, so a bidirectional connector needs both.
add_edges.name: Madeleine

remove_named_features.name: Golf
remove_named_features._comment: OSM geometry for Golf truncates ~640m short of any other graph node and sits in open ground on the SW shore of Lac de Tignes. May actually be a winter walking / dog-sled track rather than a piste. Drop entirely.

remove_named_features.name: Couloir de petite balme
remove_named_features._comment: Extreme unmaintained route across the Balme snow field. Not a marked piste — should never have been in the routing graph.

remove_named_features.name: Couloir de la Table d'orientation
remove_named_features._comment: Same family as petite balme — narrow off-piste couloir below the Bellevarde Table d'Orientation viewpoint. Its top node (alongside the high 'Face de Bellevarde top' race-start at 2804m) forms a 2-node SCC isolated from the lift area 110m below. Removing the couloir leaves the race-start as a known singleton orphan.

remove_edges._comment: The 54m link between two 'Verte bottom' nodes (Verte run terminus → 3J top) is named 'Diebold' but typed as skate, breaking the continuous Diebold piste chain that runs all the way down to Daille bottom. Drop the skate so we can add a proper run segment in its place.

53m skate named 'Run 125831' between two Coupe du Monde run segments (node 298 → Orange top 357). Same pattern as Diebold: a real piste section mis-tagged as skate, breaks the continuous Coupe du Monde piste chain.

Flat connector between Madeleine Express bottom (97) and Madeleine bottom (225). Currently a 17m skate named 'Madeleine'. Replacing with a proper run so it renders as a piste — the real-world piste runs across this 87m gap. Direction 1 of 2.

Synthetic reverse-skate between Madeleine bottom (225) and Madeleine Express bottom (97). Replacing with a piste-typed reverse so the connection is symmetrical and renders as a piste in both directions. Direction 2 of 2.
